templates.pattern: A linear search is performed on an unsorted list of [N] items. Calculate the maximum number of comparisons needed in the worst case.
templates.explanation:
Linear search worst case = n comparisons
= [N]
= [RESULT]

In the worst case the target item is the last one or not in the list at all. Every item must be checked. Linear search has O(n) time complexity.

templates.pattern: A bubble sort is performed on a list of [N] items. Calculate the maximum number of passes needed to fully sort the list.
templates.explanation:
Bubble sort max passes = n − 1
= [N] − 1
= [RESULT]

Each pass bubbles the largest unsorted element to its correct position. After n−1 passes all elements are in order. The last element is automatically in position.

templates.pattern: A bubble sort is performed on a list of [N] items. Calculate the maximum number of comparisons in the worst case.
templates.explanation:
Bubble sort max comparisons = n(n−1) ÷ 2
= [N] × ([N]−1) ÷ 2
= [N] × [N-1] ÷ 2
= [RESULT]

This is the sum 1+2+3+...+(n-1). Bubble sort has O(n²) time complexity in the worst case — it is inefficient for large lists.

templates.pattern: A stack initially contains [START] items. [PUSH] items are pushed onto the stack and [POP] items are popped off. Calculate the number of items remaining on the stack.
templates.explanation:
Items remaining = initial items + pushed items − popped items
= [START] + [PUSH] − [POP]
= [RESULT]

A stack follows LIFO — Last In First Out. Push adds to the top and pop removes from the top. A stack underflow error occurs if you try to pop from an empty stack.

templates.pattern: A queue initially contains [START] items. [ENQ] items are enqueued and [DEQ] items are dequeued. Calculate the number of items remaining in the queue.
templates.explanation:
Items remaining = initial + enqueued − dequeued
= [START] + [ENQ] − [DEQ]
= [RESULT]

A queue follows FIFO — First In First Out. Items join at the rear and leave from the front. Queues are used in print spooling, CPU scheduling and breadth-first search.

templates.pattern: An array starts at base index [BASE]. Calculate the index of the element that is [POS] positions from the start.
templates.explanation:
Array index = base index + position
= [BASE] + [POS]
= [RESULT]

Most programming languages use 0-based indexing so the first element is at index 0. Some languages like Pascal use 1-based indexing. Always check which convention is being used.

templates.pattern: A nested loop has an outer loop that runs [N] times and an inner loop that runs [M] times for each outer iteration. Calculate the total number of iterations.
templates.explanation:
Total iterations = outer loop × inner loop
= [N] × [M]
= [RESULT]

Nested loops multiply their iteration counts. Two nested loops each running n times give n² total iterations — this is why nested loops produce O(n²) algorithms.

templates.pattern: A loop starts at [START] and increments by [STEP] each iteration until it reaches [END]. Calculate the number of iterations the loop executes.
templates.explanation:
Iterations = (end − start) ÷ step
= ([END] − [START]) ÷ [STEP]
= [END-START] ÷ [STEP]
= [RESULT]

Counting loop iterations precisely is essential for calculating algorithm time complexity. Always check whether the loop condition is strict (<) or inclusive (<=).

templates.pattern: A bubble sort performs [K] complete passes on a list of [N] items. Calculate the total number of array element accesses made during these passes.
templates.explanation:
Array accesses = items × passes × 2 (read and write per comparison)
= [N] × [K] × 2
= [RESULT]

Each comparison in bubble sort accesses two array elements. Minimising array accesses is important for cache efficiency in modern processors.

templates.pattern: A selection sort is performed on a list of [N] items. Calculate the total number of comparisons made.
templates.explanation:
Selection sort comparisons = n(n−1) ÷ 2
= [N] × ([N]−1) ÷ 2
= [N] × [N-1] ÷ 2
= [RESULT]

Selection sort always makes the same number of comparisons regardless of the input order. It has O(n²) time complexity but makes fewer swaps than bubble sort.
